notes.title: Static Dread: The Lighthouse (PC) Review
notes.content:
Static Dread: The Lighthouse was a small case of mistaken identity for me. In my haste to look it over before reviewing, the screenshots made it seem like more of an interactive novel-style puzzle game with some horror elements. Imagine my surprise when it revealed itself as more of a lighthouse management game—with horror elements—which is something I’ve been dying for someone to make.

There’s such a compelling idea in exploring the terror of isolation, compounded by the responsibility of manning something as critical to other people’s survival as a lighthouse. There are so many interesting ways to create tension and a sense of paranoia. And while Static Dread: The Lighthouse doesn’t fully achieve these things, it offers a number of compelling ideas that make it a captivating experience.

Static Dread: The Lighthouse places the player in the role of a Lighthouse Keeper, newly assigned to a remote island outpost after a strange phenomenon has occurred across the world. An... Read more

notes.title: Nautical horror game Static Dread is like a Lovecraftian Papers Please
notes.content:
Lighthouses are bad news, everybody knows that. Just ask Jack from Bioshock. Or Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe in The Lighthouse. Or Lena from Annihilation. Across all media-just take those mainstream examples from games, films, and literature respectively-lighthouses are creepy and filled with incomprehensible horror. Static Dread The Lighthouse follows in the eerie footsteps of Bioshock and Dredge with its own spin on the creepy lighthouse genre, mixing Papers, Please style gameplay with old school graphics and that eldritch Lovecraftian horror.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Play Static Dread on Steam Next Fest
notes.content:
We’re celebrating [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/nextfest_feb2025]Steam Next Fest[/url] with the new update!

The tides are shifting, and the lighthouse calls once more 👁

After the playtest we received a lot of feedback and comments. Thanks to everyone who played and shared their opinion 💚 We've listened to you, and brought new life (and terror) to Static Dread with a major update! From eerie new events to tools that might just keep you sane, the darkness has never been more unpredictable. Will you survive the changes?

Here’s what awaits you:
- Full gamepad and steamdeck support.
- Rebalanced energy and sanity system. Your consciousness and sanity are now more dependent on the light. Keep the beacon burning to stay sane!
- Rebalanced sound volumes + new sounds.
- 11 bonus tracks for cassette player.
- New UI with frame-by-frame animations and improved artwork.
- Rebalanced store prices.
- The lamp, cassette player and coffee pot are now interactive and help you stay sane. The lamp creates an area of safe light where you can hide from the darkness. Cassette player helps you restore energy. Once every 4 minutes you can drink coffee from the coffee pot without spending resources.
- Many new events. Darkness became more inventive. Shadows now apper inside and outside the lighthouse, and doors have a life of their own.
- Several bug fixes.
- Additional text proofreading and correction of mistakes.

The lighthouse stands ready, its beacon cutting through the growing darkness. But the shadows are deeper now, and the whispers louder. Will you keep the light burning, or will the tides claim you too? 🌊

Dive into the update and let us know how you fare! The abyss awaits.

notes.title: Playtest is over
notes.content:
First Static Dread Playtest is Over – And It Was Awesome!

A huge thank you to everyone who participated! 780 players joined the playtest, and 300 of you filled out feedback forms. Not bad, right? This is incredibly valuable information for us.

Yeah, we get it — having to constantly run for fish, energy drinks, and coffee was exhausting. Sorry about that! :)  Oh, and the generator? Yeah, it got a little out of hand. It was way too loud, we hear you!  

We're working on improving technical stability, completely reworking the energy mechanic, and refining many aspects of the game based on your feedback.  

But you know what? Beyond all the suggestions and reports on what we need to fix, there was something else really important in your responses: the ratings you gave the game, its atmosphere, and its story. Across the board, Static Dread scored an average of 4.5 out of 5. We saw a lot of perfect scores, and many of you really, really enjoyed the experience.  

We understand that this is an early playtest, and your high ratings are a show of faith in us. The game is far from finished, but we're truly grateful for your support and excited that Static Dread is resonating with you.  

Some of the updates — like the new energy system — will be available in the Steam Next Fest demo, starting on February 24. If you played the current version, we’d love to hear your thoughts on the changes!  

Want to stay in touch? Join our Discord: [url=https://discord.gg/qC8StYqy]https://discord.gg/qC8StYqy[/url]

And if you liked the game, share it with friends, drop them a link, and ask them to wishlist it on Steam. We’d really appreciate it!

See you in Discord or at Steam Next Fest!
